summary: Implemented the PH-349 PostgreSQL multi-connection concurrency acceptance slice at BASE a5ba2fd. tests/test_v1_pg_concurrency.py contains (a) a CLI/probe runner aligned with PH-345: --dsn/PMO_PG_DSN/DATABASE_URL resolution, JSON evidence envelope (script/contract_version/mode/profile/app_sha/started_at/finished_at/exit_code/status/checks/artifacts/redactions/notes), frozen exit-code mapping (0 pass, 2 not_run/prerequisite, 3 assertion fail, 4 environment fail, 5 security reject), with a safe dry_run default, execute authorization/profile gate and exit 5 security rejection, and (b) real PostgreSQL probes that create a random isolated schema and drop it: company advisory-lock serialization (V1-OPS-06.1), concurrent unique receipt for the same org+request_token (06.2), append-only trigger rejection of UPDATE/DELETE (06.3), opposite-order locking deadlock detection plus rollback retry success (06.4). SQLite or non-PostgreSQL DSNs are rejected with exit 2 and never treated as concurrency evidence; missing DSN yields not_run; unreachable PG yields exit 4. The module also provides always-runnable contract tests (envelope shape/status mapping, missing/SQLite/non-PG DSN rejection, CLI exit 2 envelopes, unreachable PG exit 4) and a PG probe test class that skips with an explicit not_run reason when no real DSN is configured. CLI mode/security is tested: default dry_run needs no execute permission, execute without --allow-execute and execute on a production profile both return exit 5 before I/O, and dry_run on an unreachable PG returns exit 4. docs/engineering/pg-concurrency.md documents invocation, probe matrix, envelope, exit codes, isolation/redaction rules, business-level PG suites and the honest current not_run status. No production data was touched; no business tables, migrations, code paths or contracts were changed.

deviations: Execute-mode envelope fix (reviewer blocker): run_probes() now passes mode='execute' on both the success envelope and the connection-failure (exit 4) envelope, so a real execute run cannot record the dry_run default. Regression tests cover the CLI execute path with an unreachable PG (exit 4, mode=execute) and run_probes connection failure (mode=execute); scoped tests are now 14 (13 contract pass + 1 PG skip).

Review-blocker fix (old->new): the CLI now implements the full PH-345 mode/security contract — `--mode dry_run|execute` with safe `dry_run` default (read-only version check, no schema/DDL), `execute` requires explicit `--allow-execute` and a profile in {ci, staging, rehearsal}; production/unauthorized profiles or a missing allow flag return exit 5 security rejection before connecting or executing DDL, and the envelope records the actual mode. Probe assertions were strengthened: 06.1 now asserts the waiter does not acquire before release and the final order is [first, second]; 06.3 requires SQLSTATE P0001 from the append-only trigger (not any exception); artifacts record PG version and max_connections. Contract tests cover execute-without-allow, production-profile rejection, default dry_run and dry_run unreachable PG exit 4 (12 scoped tests: 11 pass, 1 PG skip).

Real PostgreSQL was not available locally, so the PG probe test is skipped with an explicit not_run reason; the slice delivers the executable probe/CLI and contract tests, not a local PG pass. Real PG evidence is delegated to CI/deployment and must not be replaced by SQLite.

No scripts/ops/* file was created because the BASE PH-349 allowed_paths only include tests/test_v1_pg_concurrency.py/docs; the executable runner is therefore the test module CLI (`python -m tests.test_v1_pg_concurrency --dsn ...`), which produces the same PH-345 envelope and exit codes.
The probe file uses psycopg3 (the installed PostgreSQL driver) directly with random throwaway schemas and no business tables; it does not modify applied migrations or production data.

Business-level concurrency (double approval, over-clearance, refunds, allocation, opening balances, close, invoice reversal, FX snapshots) is covered by existing owner concurrency suites on PG; this slice adds infrastructure probes (lock/idempotency/append-only/deadlock) and documents the business-set linkage rather than duplicating those suites.

Full-suite first run showed a transient delivery_execution heartbeat failure; it passed in isolation and in the rerun, and the stable full-run failure set equals the clean main baseline (5F+3E), so it is recorded as pre-existing flakiness, not a new regression.
